lessonRef.unitTitle: PF7 — Paying Taxes: Taxes, Take-Home Pay, and Your First Forms
lessonRef.title: Comparison and analysis: integrating PF1-PF7 into one plan

objective: Assemble a single fictional annual plan that carries income, taxes, spending, saving, credit, investing, and protection together, and check that it balances.
scenario: A fictional worker earning $44,000 builds one simulated annual plan. The tax schedule is the simplified fictional one used in this unit and every figure is invented.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional income and plan figures in these directions

tasks.directions: Gross income is $44,000. Under the fictional federal schedule, taxable income is gross less a $9,000 standard deduction, then 10% on the first $10,400 of taxable income and 12% above it. Payroll tax is 7.65%, state income tax 4.25%, and city income tax 1%, all charged on gross with no deduction.

prompts.text: What is the federal income tax?
What do payroll, state, and city taxes come to together?
What is take-home income for the year?

tasks.directions: The plan allocates take-home pay as follows: essential spending $21,600, debt repayment $2,640, emergency reserve $2,400, long-horizon investing $3,600, and insurance premiums $1,860.

prompts.text: What do the five allocations total?
How much of take-home pay is unallocated?
What percentage of gross income goes to tax? Round to one decimal place.

tasks.directions: Write the plan up as one page.

prompts.text: Present the plan and show how each of the seven topics from this course appears in it. Say what the $2,232 unallocated should do, and name the one line you would cut first if income fell 10%.

remediation: If take-home comes out near $40,000, only the federal tax has been subtracted. Total the four taxes first — $3,992.00, $3,366.00, $1,870.00, and $440.00 — and take the whole $9,668.00 off gross before any allocation. Note that only the federal line gets the $9,000 deduction.
extension: Rebuild the plan on $39,600 of gross income, keeping the reserve and insurance lines intact, and state which two lines absorbed the fall.
